subject: Plan alignment and fallback: Pinewell packaging questions
messages:
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@pinewell.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@pinewell.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify upgrade/downgrade paths and credits for pilot

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked how Redwood handles fallbacks between 'compact' and 'throughput' tiers — but before we lock in the pilot we need a clear playbook for:

- How an upgrade mid-quarter impacts committed credits vs metering (if we buy extra capacity, how are overage credits applied?)
- Downgrade windows and prorated refunds (what counts as a valid reason to step down without penalty?)
- If we enable feature-bundles (priority routing, KV cache snapshotting), can those be toggled without contract amendments?

I attached a short list of our expected traffic patterns and compliance needs (pinewell_requirements.pdf). Can you outline 2 recommended paths (Conservative pilot -> Scale; and Aggressive pilot -> Pause/Stepdown) with responsibilities and timing? Procurement wants something we can include in our SOW.

Appreciate it — Alex
Head of AI Platform, Pinewell Health

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@pinewell.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade/downgrade paths and credits for pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. I've sketched two playbooks below and attached a tailored proposal (redwood-proposal-v3.pdf):

1) Conservative pilot -> Scale (recommended for regulated workloads)
- Initial commitment: Compact tier + KV caching bundle for 3 months (committed tokens + 30% reserved throughput).
- Upgrade path: mid-quarter upgrades are allowed once per 30-day window. Additional committed capacity purchases convert to credit buckets that apply pro-rata across remaining days in the billing cycle.
- Credits/Overage: Any committed capacity top-up is applied as a prepaid credit (non-refundable) but unused credits can be rolled forward for 60 days. Overage beyond committed+credits will be metered at public metering rates.
- Downgrade: Allowed at month boundary with 14 days notice; prorated credit carry-forward applies as above. Emergency step-downs for compliance reasons can be granted by Support with a documented incident and will trigger credit review.

2) Aggressive pilot -> Pause/Stepdown (recommended for cost-sensitive experiments)
- Initial commitment: Metered compact tier with optional burst credits.
- Upgrade path: Instant upgrades to throughput tier available but billed as metered usage plus temporary premium (single billing period) unless converted to a committed reserve within 14 days.
- Credits/Refunds: No refunds for metered usage; when converting to a commitment we apply a one-time conversion credit equal to 50% of prepurchased burst spend (applies only once per deal).
- Downgrade: Immediate downgrade supported; past committed credits are forfeited if conversion to committed capacity happened less than 30 days ago.

Feature toggles: Bundled features (priority routing, KV cache snapshotting, extended observability) are configurable at route-level and do not require contract amendments for trial volumes (<= 100k tokens/day). Larger, account-wide toggles (e.g., guaranteed dedicated pool) require a formal amendment.

Next steps:
- Ben can confirm the discounting ladder and whether Pinewell's expected profile qualifies for a 10% partner discount vs our standard 5%.
- If that looks good, I'll prepare an SOW appendix with explicit day-of-month boundaries and the canary rollback wording for the SOW.

Attaching the proposal and a short comparison table in the PDF. Let me know what procurement needs as a minimum for SOW language.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v3.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@pinewell.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade/downgrade paths and credits for pilot

Alex — quick note on pricing/discounts:

- Given the projected 3mo pilot with a plausible scale to a 12mo committed expectation (per Sofia's Conservative path), Pinewell qualifies for our Standard Partner Ladder: 5% at pilot commit, 8% at 6mo sustained average, 12% at enterprise bundle commit (annual).
- For the SOW we can include a 30-day conversion credit: if you convert any metered upgrade into a committed reserve within 30 days, Redwood will apply a conversion credit equal to 25% of the metered spend that month. That sits between the Conservative (prepaid credit carry-forward) and Aggressive (50% one-time) approaches.
- Exception asks (e.g., refundable credits or rollback rebates) need a leadership signoff; Jordan I've cc'd for approval on any rebate language.

If it's helpful I can draft a short clause for procurement describing the conversion credit and the downgrade guardrail language.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Porter <alex.porter@pinewell.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade/downgrade paths and credits for pilot

Ben — approved to include the 30-day conversion credit at 25% for this pilot. A couple of governance items we need in the SOW appendix:

- Clear definition of "conversion" (signed amendment or HA-driven console toggle + invoice change).
- Maximum of one conversion credit per rolling 90-day window (to avoid repeated gaming).
- Emergency compliance step-downs: Support will issue a step-down ticket and we will provide a credit review within 10 business days. If Pinewell wants an expedited review we can offer a manual pro-rata refund subject to leadership approval (documented exception).

Sofia — please incorporate these bullets into the SOW appendix and send the updated PDF; procurement will need the exact wording on the conversion trigger and what supporting artifacts constitute an incident for emergency step-down.

Jordan Blake
VP, GTM Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@pinewell.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@pinewell.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify upgrade/downgrade paths and credits for pilot

Team — thanks, this is helpful and exactly the level of detail our Procurement asked for. A couple of small asks before we finalize SOW:

1) Can the 30-day conversion credit be split 50/50 between credits and a short-term invoice rebate? Procurement prefers some immediate cash relief to show in our pilot month budget.
2) For emergency step-downs, list the minimum artifacts we must submit (e.g., incident postmortem link + SOC contact). I'll propose specific language to Procurement once Sofia sends the amended appendix.

If you can share an updated redlined SOW appendix by EOD Wednesday (2026-10-07), we can route to our Legal and finish signature next week.

Thanks — Alex
